To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of mechanized gait training in patients in the first week after stroke allows for earlier restoration of gait and standing balance.

the complex use reflex kinesitherpy and robot driven mechanotherapy in patients of the acute period of the stroke allowed to increase the functional activities of the patients and the level of their self service already prior to the hospital discharge.

the use of mechanotherapy and robot-driven gait training in patients in the early stages of stroke leads to a significant improvement of motor function of the lower extremities and the level of functional activity of the patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a modern approach to gait retraining in patients in the early period of stroke.
the development of the modern approach to the rehabilitation of the patients in the acute phase of stroke, which is based on the use of mechanotherapy and reflex kinesitherapies.
the development and application of new methods for the rehabilitation of neurological diseases, in particular stroke, which is a major cause of disability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
robot-assisted gait rehabilitation in patients with acute stroke is effective and safe, and that it should be used in the acute phase of stroke.
this study was a good attempt to use a new method in the rehabilitation of stroke.
the use of robot driven gait trainers in the acute period after stroke is safe and efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of mechanotherapy in the early post-stroke period is a promising direction in the restoration of gait function.
a robot-driven mechanized training can be a useful tool in the rehabilitation of patients with stroke, but the evidence is still limited and further studies are needed.
robot-driven mechanotherapy is an effective method to improve gait function in patients in the early stages of cerebral stroke.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the complex use in patients with stroke of mechanized gait trainer Motomed Viva2 and GaitTrainer 1 (GT-1) allows to achieve a positive effect on the functional status of patients and to reduce the time of hospital treatment.

the complex use reflex kinesitheraphy and robot-driven mechanized therapy allows to increase the level of functional activity of patients with stroke and to restore their gait prior to discharge from hospital.

the early introduction of robot-driven gait training in patients in the early period of stroke is effective in terms of improving the functional status of patients and reducing the number of complications.
